title: C#
subtitle: A modern, statically typed language for the .NET platform, from a first file-based program to async services, LINQ and the tools professionals use every day.
description: C# (say "C sharp") is a general-purpose, statically typed language created at Microsoft and first shown in 2000. It runs on .NET, a free, open-source and cross-platform runtime, and it is used for web services and APIs with ASP.NET Core, cloud and enterprise systems, desktop applications, developer tools, and games, most famously through the Unity engine. It began as an object-oriented language in the family of C++ and Java and has grown, release by release, into one that also leans on functional ideas: records, pattern matching, LINQ and immutable data.

This course is for anyone who has finished the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or has equivalent experience: you know what a variable, a loop and a function are, in any language. It goes from installing the .NET SDK and running a one-file program to types, classes and records, generics, nullable reference types, LINQ, exceptions, async code, memory and performance, and the ecosystem of NuGet packages, tests and formatters, ending with a complete program written the way a professional team would write it. It teaches C# 14 on .NET 10, the long-term-support release.

To run the examples, install the .NET 10 SDK from the [official download page](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download) (Windows, macOS and Linux) and run any single file with `dotnet run hello.cs`. Microsoft does not offer a standalone online playground for C#; community sites such as [SharpLab](https://sharplab.io/) and [.NET Fiddle](https://dotnetfiddle.net/) let you try short snippets in a browser. Every complete program in these lessons was compiled and run with the .NET 10 SDK, and the output shown is the output it printed.

levels.title: The language and its toolchain
levels.summary: Install .NET, run your first file-based programs, and learn C#'s types, operators, control flow, methods and everyday collections.

levels.title: Modelling and querying data
levels.summary: Design types with classes, structs, records, properties, interfaces and generics, make null safe with nullable reference types and pattern matching, and query data with LINQ.

levels.title: Production C#
levels.summary: Handle failure with exceptions and deterministic cleanup, write asynchronous and allocation-aware code, and work with NuGet, ASP.NET Core, tests and analyzers on a complete project.
